claims.text: Adding 2 at.% boron to the refractory high-entropy alloy will cause boride precipitates to form.
The boride precipitates will pin dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by boride precipitates will reduce dislocation mobility.
Reduced dislocation mobility will increase the alloy's strength.
Adding 2 at.% boron will improve high-temperature yield strength by 15% relative to the as-cast alloy without boron.
The predicted high-temperature improvement will hold from 800 to 1000°C under loading conditions of 100 to 500 MPa.
Adding 2 at.% boron will increase density by less than 1% relative to the alloy without boron.
Adding 2 at.% boron will cause no significant change in room-temperature performance.

contradictions.description: The predicted yield-strength improvement is 15%, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below a 10% improvement. Results from 10% to less than 15% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying it.
The predicted density increase is less than 1%, but falsification occurs only when it exceeds 2%. An increase from 1% through 2% would violate the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
